title: Batch eviction–kernel selection mismatch incident retro and durable fixes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Executive summary: On 2026-03-09 we observed a sustained tail-latency and throughput regression in hosted inference for mixed-length conversational workloads after a scheduler change that adjusted batch eviction thresholds. The root cause was an interaction between the new eviction heuristic and kernel selection logic, which caused frequent kernel compatibility fallbacks and expensive attention reorders for long-prefix requests. This ticket captures the postmortem notes, timeline, technical root cause, short-term mitigations, and durable action items.
postmortem_summary: Impact: 6 hours of elevated p95/p99 latencies for affected customers (approx 2% of calls), visible across 4 regions. During the window we saw up to 3x increase in p99 for generation endpoints using the Llama-variant family with long prefix caching. Immediate rollback of the scheduler change restored baseline behavior. We declare this a regression introduced by runtime-1.22 scheduler tuning that didn't fully account for kernel variant affinities for mixed-length batches.

impact: Affected customers: subset of hosted API customers with mixed short/long sequence patterns using models with multiple compiled kernel variants. Observable metrics: p95 increased by ~60%, p99 by up to 3x. Throughput per-GPU dropped by ~25% during peak. No data loss or security exposure. Some enterprise customers experienced SLA blips and submitted support tickets.
root_cause: Two changes combined: (1) a scheduler tuning that lowered the batch-eviction threshold to reduce latency for short-sequence workloads, and (2) the runtime's kernel-selector assumes stable KV-cache and batch composition. Lowering eviction increased the churn of cache prefixes in mixed workloads, causing many requests to be evaluated with a kernel that lacked optimized attention kernels for long prefixes. The kernel-selector then repeatedly fell back to a less optimal kernel and triggered attention reordering paths that are orders-of-magnitude slower for those sequences. There was insufficient test coverage for mixed-length caching churn and the integration regression was not caught by staging performance tests.
short_term_mitigation: Rolled back the scheduler eviction tuning (runtime-1.22 revert) within 2 hours. Enabled a temporary runtime guard that forces kernel-selection to prefer compatibility with cached prefix lengths when eviction churn > 20%. Throttled scheduled deploys for runtime-1.22 until after remediation.
monitoring_changes: Emit kernel_selection_path tags in trace spans so we can filter requests that fall back to compatibility kernels
Add an alert: kernel_fallback_rate > 1% for 5m for models with KV-cache enabled
Add dashboard: per-GPU throughput vs eviction churn correlated view

technical_decisions: We will avoid coupling eviction thresholds to single global tuning; instead, eviction heuristics will be workload-aware (per-model and per-customer flags). Kernel-selector will adopt a 'compatibility-preserving' scoring change for 1.22.x and be revisited for a more optimal approach in 1.23. We decided against permanently raising eviction thresholds globally because that would harm short-sequence latency for many customers. Trade-off: temporary slight increase in short-tail latency for better worst-case stability.
followups: Post-deploy slo validation: run 72-hour validation window after kernel-selector changes and report to PM and SRE
Customer communication: draft and send incident summary to affected customers with remediation timeline (owner: Customer Success)
Architecture review: schedule a deeper architecture session on kernel-eviction-scheduler interplay (owner: Research/Applied ML)
